## The question {background-color="#0E1016"}

::: {.fragment}
How do customer type, store, and time of day shape what Brew & Bytes sells, and at what price?
:::
::: {.fragment}
One year, five stores, `r format(5634, big.mark = ",")` transaction lines.
:::

## One file, one command

- The analysis lives in `.qmd` files.
- Rendering runs every chunk and rebuilds every number and chart.
- The web page, the PDF and these slides come from the same source.
- Change the data, render again, and everything updates.

## The morning rush

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5
library(tidyverse)
cafe <- read_csv("data/cafe_transactions.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(!is.na(unit_price))
cafe |>
  mutate(hour = as.integer(substr(as.character(time), 1, 2))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, fill = customer_type)) +
  geom_bar() +
  facet_wrap(~store, nrow = 1)
```

## Price is set by the menu

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5
ggplot(cafe, aes(x = category, y = unit_price, fill = category)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~customer_type)
```

## A live code slide

```{r}
#| echo: true
cafe |>
  group_by(store) |>
  summarise(avg_price = mean(unit_price), lines = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(avg_price))
```

## Slide features worth knowing

- Press `S` for speaker notes, `O` for the overview, `F` for full screen.
- `incremental: true` reveals bullets one at a time.
- `{background-color="..."}` on a heading styles that one slide.
- Change `theme: simple` to `theme: moon` and render: a different deck in one word.
